How to read this page

Every part of the reference page has a fixed place. When looking up a class, read the property table first to see what you can pass at construction, then the method details to see how to call it. The table below explains what each remaining section answers, and why some tables only appear on a couple of class pages.

SectionContent
Property tableFields declared by the class itself: property name / type / default / description. When constructing an object, pass these names directly in the Class:New{ ... } table.
Inherited propertiesFields the class does not redeclare but inherits from its parent class; shown collapsed, with the class they come from.
Universal keysDeclared by no class yet accepted by every control: structure keys parent / children / name / classname / clientWidth / clientHeight, geometry keys x / y / width / height / right / bottom (from Control down). The full tables live on Object (structure keys) and Control (structure + geometry keys) only; the other 26 class pages just carry a one-line pointer - the keys are identical for every control, so repeating them 28 times would only make the page longer. Full rules: What you can pass to New.
Class indexAll 28 classes side by side: parent, own / total properties, own / total methods, skin blocks and a one-line purpose - use it to pick the class you need, then open the details. See the class index.
Properties x methodsAnswers the two questions people ask most: is a property only valid for some methods (no - every property is readable and writable on any instance), and which fields does a method read or write (a per-class method -> fields table produced by static scanning). See Properties x methods.
Method fieldsThe chips under every method detail ("fields read / written in the source") are not a property list: they are a static scan of the self.x / obj.x references inside that function body - r = read, w = written, rw = both, a leading _ means a framework-internal field. They only cover the fields the method touches directly, which is why the list looks partial. Full explanation, legend, limits and the difference from the property table: Fields read and written.
SkinsThe actual fields of all 11 bundled skins, the three ways to switch (global / per class / per control), writing your own set, and why changing the theme does not restyle existing controls. Guide: Skins; runnable demo: chili_demo_09_skins.lua.
Methods / FunctionsClass:Method(...) denotes an instance method (called with a colon; self is passed automatically and omitted from the parameter list); Class.Static(...) denotes a static function called with a dot. Every function lists its parameters and return value.
EventsProperties named On* are event tables; write them as OnClick = { function(self) ... end } at construction. When the event fires, every function in the table is called in order.
Init timingThe widget file body runs at the load stage (at that point WG.Chili is still nil); the class table only exists after api_chili.lua has been initialized. Widgets are initialized in ascending layer order, so a widget that uses Chili must set layer to > 1000.
VisibilityA top-level control must set parent = Chili.Screen0. Object:New only calls AddChild when a parent is present; an orphan control is never drawn and never receives mouse input.
Helper modulesGlobal / table functions in Handlers/, Headers/, core.lua and Themes/ that do not belong to a control class.
SkinThe per-control skin fields (color, texture, font, ...) in Skins/*/skin.lua; they decide the actual appearance of each control.

Basic usage

Chili is loaded by LuaUI/Widgets/api_chili.lua: it puts the whole class table into WG.Chili, does not create a global Chili, and has layer = 1000. That leads to three rules you must respect:

  1. Do not grab classes at file top level: the widget file body runs at the "load stage", before the framework has run Initialize, so WG.Chili is nil.
  2. layer must be greater than 1000: widgets are initialized in ascending layer order and api_chili.lua is 1000, so your own window widget must come after it.
  3. Top-level controls must pass parent: Object:New only calls AddChild when a parent is present; a control without one is not attached to Screen0, so it is never drawn and never receives mouse input.
Minimal window widget
-- api_chili.lua puts the whole Chili class table into WG.Chili (without creating a global Chili); its own layer = 1000
function widget:GetInfo()
  return { name = "Chili Test", layer = 1001, enabled = true } -- 1001 > 1000, ensuring Chili is ready first
end

local Chili, win   -- file top level only declares variables, does not grab classes

function widget:Initialize()
  Chili = WG.Chili                          -- do not use the global Chili; it does not exist
  if not Chili then return end              -- bail out if the framework failed to load, to avoid nil index

  win = Chili.Window:New{
    parent  = Chili.Screen0,                -- KEY: a control without parent is never drawn
    caption = "Example Window",
    x = 100, y = 100, width = 320, height = 180,
    children = {                            -- children automatically AddChild; do not repeat parent
      Chili.Label:New{ caption = "Chili", x = 12, y = 40 },
      Chili.Button:New{
        caption = "Click", x = 12, y = 90, width = 100, height = 26,
        OnClick = { function(self) Spring.Echo("clicked") end },
      },
    },
  }
end

The generic constructor behaviour is defined by Object:New / Control:New: copy every field of the passed table onto the new instance, handle children and childrenByName, and trigger the control's layout and draw-cache init. To change the appearance (colors / textures / fonts / padding), change that control's fields in the skin - see the Skin section below.

Porting to another game

This chili_old is already self-contained: its directory is not hardcoded (debug.getinfo resolves it), and it does not depend on Zero-K's LuaRules/Utilities tool layer - the missing Spring.Utilities.CopyTable, Spring.ScaledGetMouseState, Spring.GetViewSizes and Spring.Orig are provided by Headers/zkcompat.lua at the very start of framework loading (existing values are not overwritten).

Copy the sibling api_chili.lua and the whole chili_old/ directory into the target game's LuaUI/Widgets/ and you are done. For what happens when the target game already has chili/, and how to self-check after launch, see PORTING.md (porting notes).

Getting started

the framework is installed, so how do I get a window I wrote onto the screen? copy the template, edit GetInfo, build the controls in Initialize.

First, make sure the framework is running

Chili does not ship with the engine. It is two things: api_chili.lua (the loader, layer = 1000) and chili_old/ (the framework itself). Both must sit in the same folder

Goal: the files are in the right placeLuaUI/Widgets/
LuaUI/Widgets/
  api_chili.lua             -- loader, layer = 1000; it is what writes WG.Chili
  chili_old/                -- the framework: Controls/ Handlers/ Headers/ Skins/ Themes/
  chili_demo_00_template.lua -- the shipped template, copy it as your starting point
  my_widget.lua             -- your own widget, same folder

After starting the game, check three things:

  1. The widget list shows Chili Framework and it is ticked.
  2. infolog.txt has no chili-related Error.
  3. Nothing new on screen — that is normal: the framework only puts the class table into WG.Chili and draws no UI of its own.

your first window!

Step one: copy chili_demo_00_template.lua to my_widget.lua in the same folder; it is a skeleton that already runs. Step two: edit GetInfo. It carries a pile of fields; the three that actually bite are name / layer / enabled:

Goal: the engine recognises your widgetmy_widget.lua
function widget:GetInfo()
  return {
    name    = "My First Window",  -- shown in the widget list; do not reuse a name
    desc    = "my first chili window",
    layer   = 1010,               -- must be greater than 1000; api_chili.lua is 1000
    enabled = true,               -- the copied template defaults to false
  }
end

Step three: build the controls in Initialize. Goal: a window, some text and a button on screen — that is the smallest UI that works:

Goal: a window on screen with text and a buttonWindow / Label / Button
local Chili, win

function widget:Initialize()
  Chili = WG.Chili                    -- the class table is only reachable here
  if not Chili or not Chili.Screen0 then return end

  win = Chili.Window:New{
    parent  = Chili.Screen0,          -- a top-level control needs Screen0 as parent
    caption = "My first window",
    x = 200, y = 200, width = 320, height = 160,
  }
  Chili.Label:New{ parent = win, caption = "Hello Chili", x = 16, y = 40 }
  Chili.Button:New{ parent = win, caption = "Click me", x = 16, y = 80,
    OnClick = { function(self) Spring.Echo("clicked") end } }
end

Initialize runs once when the widget starts. Do not create controls in Update — that builds a new window every frame.

The rules you need to know

It is a strict constraint on the loading sequence and the object tree. Breaking any one of them will result in a blank screen or a "nil" error; the last one is the mechanism of New itself, explaining why there is no response when it is written.

  • layer must be greater than 1000. Widgets run Initialize in ascending layer order, api_chili.lua is 1000, and WG.Chili is written inside that loader's Initialize. So with a layer of 1000 or lower, WG.Chili is still nil inside your Initialize.
  • Never grab the classes at file top level. Top-level code runs during the loading phase, before any widget's Initialize. Declare local Chili there, assign it inside Initialize, and guard with a nil check.
  • A top-level control needs parent = Chili.Screen0. An object without a parent is not on the visible tree: Object:IsVisibleOnScreen() returns false immediately, so it is neither drawn nor hit-tested by the mouse.
  • The New table is just property assignment. Every key is written onto the instance; a misspelled key raises no error, it only leaves an unused field, so when "nothing happens" suspect the key name first. New does fix letter case (Caption is accepted as caption) but not spelling. Skins behave the same way: they are merged at New time, so changing theme or skinName later does not affect controls that already exist.

Running it, and reloading after an edit

Press F11 in game and tick your widget, then after each edit just run /luaui reload in the console: every widget is shut down and initialised again, no game restart needed. Goal: leave no UI behind on reload or exit — so Shutdown must dispose your top-level window, otherwise each reload stacks another copy of the old UI:

Goal: clean up your UI on reload or exitShutdown
function widget:Shutdown()
  if win then win:Dispose() end   -- Dispose recursively frees all child controls
  win = nil                       -- drop the reference to the dead object
end

After a reload Initialize runs again, so every local reference (win, statusLabel, ...) is reassigned; you do not need to reset anything by hand.

Where to look up a field or method name

Pick the entry point that matches what you are stuck on; it beats scrolling:

  1. "Which class should this UI use?" Class index
  2. "What keys can I put in the New table?" Keys for New
  3. "Which fields does this method touch?" Fields read and written
  4. You only remember a word → the search box (Ctrl+K)

Key names in the docs match the source, and Lua is case-sensitive: do not "tidy up" the capitalisation when copying.

What you can pass to New?

**what keys can you actually put into Class:New{...}?**

The short answer: the class's own properties + the ones it inherits + a set of keys every control understands (structural keys, geometry keys, clientWidth, ...). Those generic keys are documented nowhere else — they are all here.

1. Structural keys: parent/children/name

The short version: where a control lives, what it is called and what sits inside it are all settled in the New table — you never call AddChild yourself.

What you want: build a window, mount it on the screen, give it a name and two child controls, in one call.

Goal: window/name/child controlsWindow
local win = Window:New{
  parent = Chili.Screen0,   -- required for a top-level control, else it is an orphan
  name   = "mainwin",       -- later: win:GetChildByName("mainwin")
  x = 120, y = 90, width = 420, height = 280,
  children = { Button:New{ x = 8, y = 8, width = 80, height = 24 } },
}
KeyWhat it doesIf omitted
parentThe control it hangs under; same as calling parent:AddChild(self) right after constructionAn orphan: never drawn, never gets the mouse. Top-level controls need Chili.Screen0
childrenArray of child controls {a, b, c}; the order is the stacking order (later ones on top)No children. Writing it as a key/value table fails silently
nameControl name, used by GetChildByName and debug outputAuto-generated as "classname + counter". A duplicate name under the same parent raises an error
classnamePicks which skin applies (skin[classname])The class's own classname
clientWidth / clientHeightSize of the client area (where content may draw); the framework adds padding back to get width / heightComputed as width / height minus padding
minimumSizeOld form {w, h}, equivalent to minWidth + minHeightnil, so the minWidth / minHeight defaults apply

The six size/position keys (x / y / width / height / right / bottom) are the next section. Iterate children with ipairs(win.children), never pairs.

2. Geometry keys: fixed / pinned right / stretched / percentage

The short version: positions do not have to be pixels. Horizontally x / width / right — pick two; vertically y / height / bottom — pick two. The framework computes the one you left out.

What you want: a button of fixed size at a fixed spot.

Goal: fixed size and positionButton
local ok = Button:New{
  parent = win, x = 8, y = 232, width = 120, height = 24,
  caption = "OK",
}

What you want: a close button that always sits 8 pixels from the window's right edge.

Goal: pinned to the parent's right edgeButton
local close = Button:New{
  parent = win, right = 8, y = 8, width = 80, height = 24,
  caption = "Close",
}
-- no x given: x = parent client width - 80 - 8

What you want: an edit box glued to both edges, growing and shrinking with the window.

Goal: stretch left to rightEditBox
local bar = EditBox:New{
  parent = win, x = 8, right = 8, y = 40, height = 24,
}
-- no width given: width = parent client width - 8 - 8

What you want: a panel that is always half the window wide.

Goal: percentage of the parentPanel
local half = Panel:New{
  parent = win, x = 0, width = "50%", y = 0, height = 120,
}
-- any string is a percentage; x / y / width / height all accept it

Writing right or a percentage stores a constraint that is recomputed whenever the parent changes; a negative number measures from the right, so x = -120 means "parent width - 120".

3. three mechanisms that decide what New does!

The short version: New does not store your table as-is — it does a few things you would not guess, and those are the root cause of "I set the key and nothing happened".

① Table values are merged layer by layer, and merging only fills empty slots. Control:New loads the theme and skin first, then Object:New fills in the class defaults with table.merge; merge skips any slot that already has a value, so whatever you wrote always wins. Arrays are filled by position: padding = {10} becomes {10, 5, 5, 5}, not 10 on every side.

② Geometry keys are constraints: recorded at New time, turned into coordinates later from the parent's size. right / bottom, percentages and negative numbers all go into _relativeBounds and are recomputed when the parent resizes — that is what makes them better than hard pixels.

Why pinning right follows the window: the constraint is recomputedControl
local bar = EditBox:New{ parent = win, x = 8, right = 8, y = 40, height = 24 }
win:Resize(800, 600)   -- parent got wider, bar.width is recomputed
bar:SetPos(20)         -- a numeric x: the right constraint is dropped, it is no longer pinned

③ Case correction only covers class properties. Object:New turns your Padding into padding; but nothing corrects generic keys such as x / width / right, so a misspelling fails silently.

4. Four traps worth remembering

The short version: all four of the following look right and do nothing. The fix is right after each one.

What you want: centre a control, hide it by default, reorder its stacking, or make the content area exactly some width — none of that is a New key.

  1. There is no center / dock / anchor key. Either compute x = (win.clientWidth - 200) / 2 once the parent exists, or use a percentage like x = "25%"; for automatic layout use LayoutPanel / Grid.
  2. **visible = false in New does not work**: when the control is mounted, Object:SetParent forces visible = true. Call ctrl:Hide() after construction instead.
  3. **There is no layer key.** Stacking is just the order inside the parent's children array; use ctrl:SetLayer(5) / :BringToFront(), and the control must already have a parent.
  4. **When the parent drives your size, use clientWidth.** For a content area exactly 200 wide, set clientWidth = 200 and let the framework add padding back; hand-computing it from padding breaks as soon as the skin or font changes.

If a key seems ignored, check this section first: wrong capitalisation of a class property is corrected for you, a misspelled generic key is not — and nothing reports it.

5. Next

With the keys right, the next step is reading and writing fields on a control, and making it move with the window.

Next: reading and writing fields, and runnable examples.

Fields read and written

The details of the method are shown in the row of small squares below. The fields read and written in the source code are not parameters of the method, nor are they the attributes of this control. They only answer one question: Which fields of the control were accessed and read or written in this function's code? The parameters are in parentheses, the attributes are in the above attribute table, and the squares represent what this code has done.

Parameters live in the parentheses, fields live in the chips

Parameters are the values you pass when you call the method. Fields are properties on the control itself (width, caption, color...). The chips count the self.xxx references inside the function body.

parameters and fieldsControl:SetPos
-- x y w h in the parentheses are PARAMETERS
function Control:SetPos(x, y, w, h)
  self.width = w   -- width is a FIELD: written here
  self.x     = x   -- x is a FIELD: written here
end
-- so the chips for SetPos are: x w  y w  width w  height w  (w = written)

How it is computed

When the documentation is built (_docbuild/parse.cjs), four steps run for every function, as pure text processing (no Lua is executed):

  1. Cut out the function body: from the function line, count function/do/repeat against end until they balance.
  2. Find self.fieldName and obj.fieldName inside the body (only these two prefixes are recognised).
  3. Look at what follows the reference: a single = (not ==) counts as write w, everything else counts as read r.
  4. A field that is both read and written becomes rw.

So it is an index of "which method touches which field", not a hand-written description.

Example 1: pin a button to the right edge

What you want: the button stays on the right side of the window and follows when the window gets wider.

SetPos with hard-coded coordinates does not work: its chips contain no right, it only writes x/width. Give right to New instead.

pinned-right buttonButton
-- wrong: stops hugging the edge as soon as the window is resized
btn:SetPos(300, 10, 80, 24)

-- right: give right and width only, x is computed for you
local btn = Button:New{
  parent = win, right = 8, y = 8, width = 80, height = 24,
  caption = "Close",
}

Why: right is resolved into x in Control:DetectRelativeBounds (that method's chips do contain right rw); SetPos does not do that job. If a field is missing from the chips, that method simply does not look at it.

Example 2: why visible = false in New does nothing

What you want: build the window now, show it later.

When the control is attached to its parent, Object:SetParent writes visible to true - its chips contain visible w.

start hiddenWindow
local win = Window:New{ parent = Chili.Screen0, visible = false }  -- reset to true
win:Hide()   -- hide it after construction: this one works

Example 3: SetValue versus setting the field

What you want: set a progress bar to 50%.

set progressProgressbar
bar:SetValue(0.5)   -- chips: value rw + OnChange r -> your OnChange fires
bar.value = 0.5     -- field only, no callback
bar:Invalidate()    -- after setting the field, redraw if you want it visible now

rw means read-then-write (the typical setter); OnChange r means the method only reads that table to call it.

How to read the chips (three lines)

  • Coloured: r read-only (it will not change your value), w gets written (your value may be overwritten), rw read and written (a setter).
  • **Grey _ prefix**: framework-internal field (for example _relativeBounds), do not set it yourself.
  • No chip at all: this function touches no field directly (Control:Resize just forwards to SetPos); that does not make it useless.

Why the list looks partial

It only scans this one function body, so the following are expected, not missing data:

  • **Only self. / obj.**: win.width, parent.x and local variables such as t.width are not counted.
  • Fields changed by another method are not credited here: if A calls B, whatever B changes is listed under B. That is why Control:Resize has an empty chip row.
  • Nested tables are recorded by their first key: self.font.size is recorded as font.
  • **A whole-table table.merge counts once**: tables such as font / skin poured in at once are recorded only by the table name.

How it relates to "usable properties"

One sentence: the property table answers "what can I set on this control" (complete), the chips answer "what does this method touch" (a subset).

When is it worth watching?

  1. Which field must I set before calling a method? Look at what it reads.
  2. Why did my value get overwritten? Look at who writes it.
  3. Do I have to redraw afterwards? Look for _needRedraw or an OnChange call.

Next: to write all these keys at once in New, see What you can pass to New; to search methods by "what I want to do", see Key functions and common patterns; for the property list of a control, see Class index.

Key functions and common patterns

to change something on screen, which API do I call? Nine times out of ten the answer is in the quick table below; the rest is covered by three copy-paste patterns; and "I changed it but nothing happened" almost always means you hit one of the four mechanics at the end.

The table is organised by what you want to achieve: left is the goal, right is the code to copy.

What you wantWhich methodCopy this
open a window / close itClass:New{} / :Dispose()win = Chili.Window:New{parent = Chili.Screen0, x = 120, y = 120, width = 400, height = 300}
move / resize / read the size:SetPos(x, y, w, h); read .width / .heightwin:SetPos(200, 140, 360, 300)
hide, then show again:SetVisibility(b) / :Hide() / :Show()win:SetVisibility(false)
put one control above another:SetLayer(n) / :BringToFront() / :SendToBack()win:BringToFront()
change the displayed textLabel/Button :SetCaption(); EditBox :SetText()label:SetCaption("new text")
change colour / fontbackgroundColor, font, ... + :Invalidate()label.backgroundColor = {1, 0.8, 0.2, 1} label:Invalidate()
react to a button pressOnClick: a list of functions, several are allowedChili.Button:New{parent = win, OnClick = {function(self) ... end}}
grab a child control:GetChildByName(name) / the children arraylocal lb = win:GetChildByName("status")

Two things do not fit in a table. Scrolling: ScrollPanel:SetScrollPos(x, y) moves the viewport to (x, y) and clamps to the valid range (pass a huge y to jump to the bottom); smoothScroll = true is the default and animates, so pass forceNotSmooth = true as the fourth argument to jump immediately. Scrollbars only appear when children extend past the visible area; switch them with verticalScrollbar / horizontalScrollbar. Saving settings is not a Chili feature: widget:GetConfigData() returns a table the engine serialises into LuaUI/Config, and the engine calls widget:SetConfigData(data) the next time your widget is enabled, so just write those values back into the controls there.

Button click changes a label

Answer: put a function list in OnClick and call Label:SetCaption(); you never repaint by hand.

Goal: one click on the button and the label next to it immediately says "clicked N times".

Goal: a button that updates a Label captionLabel + Button
local count = 0
local label = Chili.Label:New{ parent = win, x = 20, y = 46, caption = "not clicked yet" }
Chili.Button:New{
  parent = win, caption = "click me", x = 20, y = 84, width = 120, height = 28,
  OnClick = {
    function(self)
      count = count + 1
      label:SetCaption("clicked " .. count .. " times")  -- does UpdateLayout + Invalidate
    end,
  },
}

Note: Label has no SetText() (that one belongs to EditBox). Assigning label.caption = "x" does not repaint: you must call :Invalidate() yourself, and because Label is autosize by default a longer or shorter text also needs :UpdateLayout() to resize the box. SetCaption() does all that for you.

Make a window draggable

Answer: Window drags out of the box, draggable already defaults to true, so there is almost nothing to write.

Goal: press any empty part of the window (not on a button) and drag the whole thing around.

Goal: a draggable, non-resizable windowWindow
win = Chili.Window:New{
  parent = Chili.Screen0,
  caption = "drag me",
  x = 120, y = 120, width = 420, height = 260,
  resizable = false,   -- no resize corner any more
  draggable = true,    -- already the default; written out for clarity
}
-- make only the skin's drag box draggable:
win.dragUseGrip = true

Note: dragging is built in. Pressing on the window calls StartDragging(), and Control:MouseMove then does SetPos(x + dx, y + dy), so do not write your own MouseMove handler to move a window. A mouse-down consumed by a button never starts a drag. tweakDraggable only matters in the engine's tweak mode, not for a normal player UI.

Refresh a HUD every frame (throttled)

Answer: accumulate dt inside widget:Update(dt) and only touch the control once an interval has passed.

Goal: a label on screen showing game time, updating five times a second is plenty and you do not want to rebuild it every frame.

Goal: one HUD line updated every 0.2sLabel + widget:Update
local acc = 0
local hud = Chili.Label:New{ parent = Chili.Screen0, x = 20, y = 40, caption = "" }
function widget:Update(dt)
  acc = acc + dt
  if acc < 0.2 then return end   -- 5 updates per second looks continuous
  acc = 0
  hud:SetCaption("time " .. math.floor(Spring.GetGameSeconds()))
end

Note: SetCaption re-measures the text and calls Invalidate(), so calling it every frame rebuilds a display list every frame and dozens of such labels will cost you FPS. HUD elements hang off Chili.Screen0; dispose them in widget:Shutdown.

Why did the change not have the desired effect?

Answer: most changes in Chili are not immediate. It caches the drawing, resolves geometric constraints into coordinates, fixes the skin at construction time, and moves hidden children into another table. Hit any of these and the API looks broken.

  1. Drawing is cached; field changes need an explicit invalidation. Controls default to useDList = true and draw themselves into an OpenGL display list. :Invalidate() only marks the control dirty and calls RequestUpdate(); the real rebuild happens in the next frame's Update. So after assigning backgroundColor, caption or similar you must call :Invalidate() yourself. Set* methods (Label:SetCaption, Progressbar:SetValue, ...) already do. Also note Invalidate on Object is an empty function; only Control implements it.
  2. **right / bottom are constraints, not fields.** After New, DetectRelativeBounds records the constraints you gave and GetRelativeBox turns right / bottom into x / width (right = 10 means 10 pixels from the parent's right edge; "100%" style values work too). When an axis has only one constraint the other end falls back to defaultWidth / defaultHeight (Object uses 10, Label uses 70) -- that is your "the width I set was ignored". SetPos(x, y, w, h) writes only these four fields and drops any earlier right / bottom constraint; w / h are clamped to minWidth / maxWidth.
  3. The skin is merged only at New time. Control:New calls theme.LoadThemeDefaults(obj) + SkinHandler.LoadSkin(obj, self), filling the instance from skin.general and skin.<ClassName>. Changing skinName or swapping the theme afterwards never re-skins the control -- either pass skinName when creating it, or Dispose() and rebuild.
  4. Hidden controls leave the children array. SetVisibility(false) goes through parent:HideChild(), which moves the control into children_hidden, so ipairs(win.children) and #win.children no longer see it (GetChildByName does search the hidden table, so it still finds it). SetParent also resets visible to true -- that is the "it reappeared after I re-parented it" effect. If you need OnShow / OnHide callbacks use Show() / Hide(); SetVisibility only flips the state and fires no events.

Next: read FAQ and pitfalls

FAQ

Use the "phenomenon" index to identify the pitfalls. First, search for the phenomenon you encountered, then look at the causes and solutions. Each item is marked with the relevant class/function. Click the link to return to the corresponding page to check the details. (The order is roughly arranged according to the probability of encountering pitfalls when beginners start.)

First three things to check

1. The window is completely invisible
  1. No parent. Object:New only calls AddChild when a parent is given; an orphan control is never drawn and gets no mouse input. A top-level window needs parent = Chili.Screen0.
  2. layer <= 1000. Widgets initialise in ascending layer order and api_chili.lua is 1000, so your Initialize ran while WG.Chili was still nil and the widget quietly returned.
  3. enabled = false. Most demo files ship disabled; tick them in the widget list or change enabled in GetInfo.

Debug order: Spring.Echo checkpoints > is WG.Chili non-nil → is win.visible true and is win.x/win.y inside the screen?

2. attempt to index global 'Chili' (a nil value)

You grabbed the class table at file scope. Widget files are executed during the load stage, before the framework exists. Declare local Chili at the top and assign Chili = WG.Chili inside widget:Initialize().

The same applies to local Window = Chili.Window — if you want such locals, create them in Initialize.

3. attempt to index field 'Screen0' (a nil value) / WG.Chili is nil

The framework did not load — not your widget's fault. Search infolog.txt for the first Error mentioning Chili Framework. Common causes: chili_old/ not next to api_chili.lua, a missing file inside chili_old/, or missing engine APIs when porting (see PORTING.md).

If both chili/ and chili_old/ are installed, the loader picks one by config. Both loaders are named Chili Framework, so only one should be active.

Nothing appears / appears wrong

1. I changed a colour or a caption and nothing repaints

Controls default to useDList = true, caching themselves in an OpenGL display list. After a direct field assignment, invalidate that cache:

Repaint after a field changeControl:Invalidate
label.caption = "new text"
label:SetCaption("new text")   -- better: Set* handles the repaint
panel.backgroundColor = {1, 0, 0, 1}
panel:Invalidate()                -- required after assigning a field

See Control:Invalidate. If the control sits inside a hidden parent, invalidating will not make it appear — show the parent.

2. I set width = 300 and the width did not change

x/y/width/height are layout constraints: each axis needs two of them to resolve, and with only one the control falls back to defaultWidth/defaultHeight.

  • x axis: x + width, or right + width, or x + right
  • y axis: y + height, or bottom + height, or y + bottom

Second common cause: the control is inside a StackPanel/Grid with resizeItems = true, so the container decides the size.

3. Everything is crammed into the top-left corner / overlapping

Child coordinates are relative to the parent's client area (title bar and border removed). When adding children to a Window, start around y = 30, or the title bar covers them. Also check for a missing y — the default is 0, which stacks everything.

Debug trick: give controls a temporary backgroundColor to see the area they really occupy.

4. My child sizes are ignored inside StackPanel / Grid

That is what resizeItems = true means: the panel divides its client area into columns × rows cells and each child fills one. A single-column StackPanel gives every child the same height and full width; a single-row one gives equal widths and full height.

For free sizing use a plain Panel with absolute coordinates, or set resizeItems = false and place children yourself.

5. Controls in a named children table never show up

Object:New only iterates the array part of children (for i = 1, #children); named keys are silently ignored. Use a plain array: children = { Chili.Label:New{...}, Chili.Button:New{...} }.

6. AddChild: a child with the name 'xxx' already exists

Object:AddChild raises an error when childrenByName already holds that name. New generates a unique name per instance (class name + counter), so collisions only happen when you hard-code name = "row" and add a second one.

Append an index to fixed names (name = "row_" .. i), or leave name out entirely.

7. Chinese (or other non-Latin) text renders as boxes

The default font is FreeSansBold.otf (see Font) and may not contain CJK glyphs. Switch to a font that does: font = { font = "YourCJKFont.otf", size = 14 }, with the font file placed where the VFS can read it (for example LuaUI/Fonts/). Also save your Lua file as UTF-8 without BOM, or the text arrives already mangled.

Events

1. My event fires during construction and the callback finds nil controls

Three classes fire events from inside New:

  • TabBar: New ends with obj:Select(selected) → one OnChange(self, tabname);
  • ComboBox: New calls obj:Select(obj.selected or 1) → OnSelect(self, idx, true);
  • TreeView: New calls obj:Select(selected or 1) → OnSelectNode(self, node, old).

So every callback that touches a control created later must nil-guard it: if not preview then return end. The demo widgets do exactly that.

2. In Checkbox's OnChange, self.checked is the old value

Checkbox:Toggle notifies listeners with the new state first and flips self.checked afterwards, so inside the callback the field still holds the previous value. Use the argument newChecked.

3. Dragging a Trackbar freezes the game / stack overflow

Almost always recursion: the OnChange handler calls trackbar:SetValue(...) and SetValue fires OnChange every time, even when the value does not change. Keep the handler to other controls, or guard the loop:

Guard the loop with a flagTrackbar OnChange
local syncing = false
trackbar.OnChange = { function(self, v)
  if syncing then return end
  syncing = true
  other:SetValue(v)      -- will fire once more, but the flag stops it
  syncing = false
end }
4. Progressbar's OnChange sometimes does not fire

Progressbar:SetValue only notifies when the value really changed (Trackbar differs — it notifies every time). This is deliberate, so per-frame updates of an unchanged value do not flood your handlers. If you need a reaction every call, do it in your own code.

5. Progressbar:SetValue(v) does not update the text

SetValue only sets the number. Set the caption explicitly with :SetCaption("60%"), or call :SetValue(v, true) to have the number written into the caption.

6. Does EditBox have an OnTextChange event?

No. Read the content with :GetText() (multi-line boxes return lines joined by \n). For live reaction use OnKeyPress, or simply read when the user confirms.

Shutdown, reload, performance

1. The window stays on screen after the widget is disabled

Shutdown never disposed the top-level window. Add it:

Dispose the window in Shutdownwidget:Shutdown
function widget:Shutdown()
  if win then win:Dispose() end
  win = nil
end

Without it the control objects stay parented to Screen0 and still receive the mouse.

2. Two windows appear after /luaui reload

You are creating the UI more than once, usually by calling build_ui() from Update or another recurring callback. Build only in Initialize, and make sure Shutdown disposes. A defensive if win then win:Dispose() end before building also works.

3. The widget is not loaded at all / gets disabled automatically

LuaUI disables widgets that throw during load or initialisation. Look in infolog.txt for [widgets.lua] Error: or Removed widget: <your name>, then scroll up to the first error, which normally carries the file and line number.

Frequent messages: "attempt to call a nil value" (misspelled method or wrong class) and "attempt to index nil" (see the entries above).

4. The UI stutters / frame rate drops
  • Do not touch controls every frame. SetCaption/SetValue re-trigger layout and repaint; throttle to 0.2–0.5 s with an accumulated timer (demo 06).
  • Skip unchanged values: if text ~= last then label:SetCaption(text); last = text end.
  • Update big lists incrementally instead of clearing and rebuilding them each frame.
  • Do not swap Image.file every frame — that reloads the texture.
5. Buttons do not receive clicks / the mouse passes through

Hit testing is rectangle-based and follows draw order: higher layers and later children get the mouse first. Check for:

  • an invisible full-size Panel on top swallowing the clicks;
  • a control positioned outside its parent's client area (clipped visually but still holding a rectangle);
  • decoration overlays that should not take input — see hitTest / disableChildrenHitTest on the base classes.
6. The window cannot be dragged or resized

Window.draggable and Window.resizable are both false by default — switch them on explicitly. Dragging a window normally means dragging its title bar; with dragUseGrip = true only the grip area works, so set it to false if "drag from anywhere" is what you want. In tweak (UI-edit) mode the relevant flags are tweakDraggable/tweakResizable.

Misc

7. How do I pin a window to the right edge / keep it there on resize?

Use relative constraints right/bottom (see the "layout constraints" section of Getting started): right = 20, width = 280, y = 20, height = 200. To re-place descendants when the window itself is resized, react to OnResize(self, cw, ch).

8. How do I debug the UI?
  • Spring.Echo plus infolog.txt;
  • dbg_chili_inspector.lua and dbg_chili_profiler.lua in the widgets folder — enable one and read its own header for usage;
  • print the tree: for i,c in ipairs(win.children) do Spring.Echo(i, c.classname, c.name, c.x, c.y) end;
  • /luaui reload re-runs your widget without restarting the game.
9. I edited the framework sources — do I need to regenerate this document?

Yes. The document is generated from source: double-click build-docs.bat in the chili_old/ folder (a Chinese-named copy of the same script sits next to it), which runs parse.cjs and rebuilds both language versions. If you only change descriptions, edit _docbuild/desc/*.json (Chinese) and _docbuild/desc_en/*.json (English).

10. Using this framework in another game

Copy api_chili.lua and the whole chili_old/ folder into the target game's LuaUI/Widgets/. Path and ZK-dependency compatibility has already been handled here (Headers/zkcompat.lua). For the full procedure, including what to do when the target already ships Chili, see PORTING.md and the porting section of this document.

Skins

how do I give the UI a different look?. The answer is to set a control's skinName (global, per class, or per control), but a skin is merged into the instance the moment it is created - so controls that are already on screen will not restyle themselves; you have to dispose and rebuild them.

1. What a skin is

Bottom line: a skin is a table returned by Skins/<dir>/skin.lua whose keys are control field names; when a control is Newed (Controls/control.lua:79-81) those values are copied onto the instance, so ctrl.textColor, ctrl.backgroundColor and ctrl.DrawControl end up as the control's own fields - a skin is not a stylesheet, it is a set of ready-made defaults.

The effect you want: stop hand-writing colours, fonts and borders for every button and let a group of controls share one look. A skin table holds three things: info (metadata, info.name is the skin's name), general (fallback fields applied to every control), and one block per class - the key is the lower-case classname, the value holds the fields to override plus the draw function DrawControl. One aside: in the bundled skins skin.control carries the same fields as skin.general (7 write the skin.control = skin.general alias line, the other 4 get it through info.depend), so when a class has no block of its own, what actually applies is general.

A skin is just a tableSkins/<name>/skin.lua
return {
  info    = { name = "Glass" },                                -- required: skin name
  general = { textColor = {1,1,1,1}, borderThickness = 1.5 },  -- applies to all controls
  button  = { DrawControl = DrawButton },                      -- key = lower-case classname
}

Note: the keys are the property names, so the textColor / backgroundColor / font / padding you want to change all live in this table - whichever field you change, write that key.

2. Three ways to choose a skin

Bottom line: all three scopes write the same field, skinName: global sets theme.skin.general.skinName, per class sets theme.skin[lowercase classname].skinName, per control just writes it in the New table. Use them together and the order is per control > per class > global.

Why that order: inside Control:New, theme.LoadThemeDefaults first merges theme.skin[classname] and then theme.skin.general, while table.merge only fills empty slots. So a value you wrote in the New table exists first and nothing can override it; general is merged last and only fills what neither of the other levels provided.

Goal: restyle everything / only buttons / only this onewidget:Initialize
-- 1) global: every control created afterwards
Chili.theme.skin.general.skinName = "Glass"

-- 2) per class: only Button changes (the key does not exist yet, create it)
Chili.theme.skin.button = Chili.theme.skin.button or {}
Chili.theme.skin.button.skinName = "Carbon"

-- 3) per control: affects this instance only
local b = Chili.Button:New{ parent = win, caption = "OK", skinName = "Twilight" }

Note: (1) the per-class key matches the exact classname: theme.skin.button only affects controls whose classname is button, and a class derived from Button does not follow it automatically - only blocks inside a skin file walk the inheritance chain. (2) A wrong name does not raise an error - GetSkin returns nil, every block of that skin is skipped and only the default skin fills in, which looks like "the skin changed but got ugly". Look names up with Chili.SkinHandler.GetAvailableSkins() instead of hard-coding them.

3. Why nothing happens after you change it (the mechanism)

Bottom line: a skin is a set of ordinary fields copied in at construction time, not a runtime stylesheet. Changing theme or ctrl.skinName afterwards has no effect, because no code reads it again.

Four facts, and you will never have to guess again:

  • There is exactly one merge point. SkinHandler.LoadSkin is called from Controls/control.lua:81 and nowhere else in the repository; there is no ApplySkin / ReloadSkin API and no "restyle" entry point.
  • **table.merge only fills empty slots** (Headers/util.lua:295-307: elseif (self[i] == nil) then self[i] = v end). Even if you merge a skin table by hand, existing colours and textures are not overwritten - only fields that are still nil get filled.
  • **skinName is read once**, on the first line of LoadSkin (GetSkin(control.skinName), Handlers/skinhandler.lua:147). Setting ctrl.skinName later just stores a string on the control.
  • Every child is merged when it is Newed; it does not inherit from its parent. So a new skin means rebuilding the whole subtree - and conversely Dispose on the parent destroys the children too, nothing leaks.
What does NOT work!neither has any effect
win.skinName = "Glass"                        -- no effect: nobody reads it after New
Chili.theme.skin.general.skinName = "Glass"   -- no effect: only new controls use it
Goal: actually change the skin at runtimedispose + rebuild
local win

local function rebuild()
  if win then win:Dispose() end                -- destroy the old tree first
  win = Chili.Window:New{ parent = Chili.Screen0, caption = "Skins",
                          x = 100, y = 100, width = 420, height = 300 }
end

Chili.theme.skin.general.skinName = "Carbon"
rebuild()                                      -- only a rebuild picks up the new skin

Note: disposing throws away the text in EditBoxes, the scroll position of ScrollPanels, and so on - save what you need into widget locals or GetConfigData() before rebuilding. During development /luaui reload is the lazy option: it re-runs every widget from scratch.

4. Write your own minimal skin

Bottom line: create Skins/<name>/skin.lua in the chili directory with info + general and it already works; add a block for any class you want to override. Classes you do not write are filled in by the default skin, so a dozen lines is enough.

Three rules you will get wrong otherwise:

  • **info.name is required:** the loader first checks that the file returns a table with a table info (Handlers/skinhandler.lua:66), then indexes it by info.name:lower() (line 69) - a missing name is not "skipped", it errors.
  • Textures are file names, not paths: at load time TranslateFilePaths tries each string in [the skin's own directory, the info.depend directories, Skins/default/] and replaces the first match with a full path; an unresolved name stays as written - at run time the texture simply does not show and nothing warns you.
  • Override only the classes you care about: BubbleBlack writes just general + window and lets default fill the rest instead of copying all 19 blocks.
Goal: a dark skin that keeps the stock button drawingSkins/MySkin/skin.lua
local skin = {
  info = { name = "MySkin" },
  general = {                            -- applies to all controls
    textColor       = {0.9, 0.95, 1, 1},
    font            = { size = 13, outline = false },
    borderThickness = 1.5,
    borderColor     = {1, 1, 1, 0.6},
    backgroundColor = {0.1, 0.12, 0.18, 0.9},
  },
  button = { DrawControl = DrawButton }, -- draw function from skinutils
}
return skin

Note: keeping the directory name equal to info.name saves trouble; skin directories are scanned once at framework load, so a new or renamed skin needs /luaui reload.

5. Next

Next: for a clickable skin-switcher UI read the skins section of the examples - the source is LuaUI/Widgets/chili_demo_09_skins.lua (it demos all three ways plus dispose-and-rebuild). To see which fields a bundled skin actually sets, see the skins chapter.

Properties x methods

Specific issue: (1) is any property valid only for some methods? (2) does a given method touch the field I care about? (3) which method should I call to change something? The method -> fields tables below are not hand-written: the builder scans each function body for reads and writes of self.x / obj.x, so they can be relied on.

Confused by the "fields read / written" chips? Read Fields read and written first: it explains that they are a static scan of self. / obj. references, not a property list, why they look partial, and what they are good for.

1. The answer: no property is restricted to certain methods

Every property is a plain field on the instance (or on the class table); methods only read and write them. There is no mechanism such as "padding is only valid for layout methods" or "backgroundColor only for drawing methods" — any inherited property can be read and written on any instance. What does differ is who consumes the value and when: fields read once during construction versus fields read on every resize / repaint.

MechanismIn the sourceWhat it means for properties
Inheritance = copyingObject:Inherit: for i,v in pairs(self) do … class[i] = v end (table fields are table.shallowcopy-ed; the setmetatable(class,{__index=self}) line is commented out)Parent fields physically exist on the child class table (no lookup delegation), so an instance naturally has every ancestor field.
Instances inherit the class chainsetmetatable(obj, {__index = self}) at the end of Object:NewA field missing on the instance falls back to the class table, i.e. the class default; writing the same key on the instance shadows it for that instance only.
Scalars are not copiedObject:New only table.merges class fields whose type(v)=="table"; the comment says "We do not need to copy other types".number / string / boolean defaults come from the class table; changing one creates a same-named key on the instance and does not affect other instances.
Table fields merge key by keytable.merge(obj[i], classDefault): fill-only (if self[i]==nil then self[i]=v end), recursing into nested tablesThe table you pass is merged key by key with the class default: padding={10} becomes {10,5,5,5}; each instance owns its own copy.
Fields read during constructionin Control:New: padding -> clientArea, minimumSize -> minWidth, classname / skinName -> skin selectionThese properties can still be written, but changing them after construction does not recompute anything — call the matching method (e.g. UpdateClientArea) or rebuild the control.

2. Three kinds of properties, by when they are read

All are writable, but whether a write takes effect immediately differs a lot. To check: open the method details and read the "fields read / written in the source" line, or use the table below.

KindTypical fieldsAfter writing
Read once at constructionpadding clientWidth clientHeight minimumSize classname skinName children parent fontAn already-built control will not recompute: for geometry use SetPos / Resize / UpdateClientArea; for skins you have to rebuild the control.
Read on every repaint / layoutbackgroundColor borderColor borderThickness font.color caption x y width height visible enabledCall :Invalidate() (repaint) or :RequestRealign() (re-layout) afterwards. For x/y/width/height prefer :SetPos() / :Resize(), which also handle right/bottom constraints and children.
Internal caches (_ prefix)_own_dlist _children_dlist _all_dlist _relativeBounds _givenBounds _realignRequestedDo not write them: methods maintain them during draw / layout, and manual writes cause wrong rendering. In this reference they are the grey chips.

3. Per class: method -> fields

Only methods declared by this class are listed; inherited methods appear under their parent. Each method lists the fields it actually reads or writes (pure forwarders / empty bodies show an em dash). Click a field name to jump to its property description; _-prefixed ones are framework internals.

4. How to use these two tables

  1. "Is this property only valid for some method?" — no. Every property is readable and writable on every instance; the difference is whether it is read once at construction or on every repaint (section 2).
  2. "Will this method re-layout?" — look for _realignRequested / _relativeBounds / _givenBounds in its field list; if present it re-lays out (usually through UpdateLayout or AlignControl).
  3. "Which method should I call to change X?" — find the method that reads that field in section 3 and call it: e.g. to let a control stretch with its parent, do not compute width yourself every frame; pass right at construction and call :Resize().
  4. Every method detail also carries a "fields read / written in the source" line — the same data for a single function.

Overview / Controls / Object

ClassObject

Defined in Controls/object.lua:3 · Parent:none (root class) · own props 26 · available properties 26 · own methods 63 · available methods 63
InheritanceObjectsubControlFontScreen

Base class of all Chili UI objects and the root of every control and container; provides parent-child hierarchy, visibility and layer ordering, listener dispatch and coordinate conversion.

Properties 26 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring'object'Class identifier string, used by InheritsFrom and for default instance names; defaults to 'object'.
defaultWidthnumber10Default width in pixels, used when width is not set explicitly; defaults to 10.
defaultHeightnumber10Default height in pixels, used when height is not set explicitly; defaults to 10.
visiblebooleantrueWhether the object is visible; defaults to true. hidden is its negated synonym field.
preserveChildrenOrderbooleanfalseWhen true, removing a child keeps the remaining order; when false, adding/removing children is faster but the children array order becomes unreliable; defaults to false.
childrentable{}Array of child controls ordered by layer; child objects and their hardlinks are also used as keys to store layer indices.
children_hiddentable{}Children detached by HideChild that still belong to this control; each value stores the saved layer index plus links to the preceding/following neighbour.
childrenByNameanyCreateWeakTable()Weak table mapping child name -> child hardlink, used by GetChildByName for fast lookup.

KeyTypeWhen omittedDescription
parentObjectnilsame as calling parent:AddChild(self) right after construction. Required for a top-level control (usually Chili.Screen0); an orphan is never drawn and never receives input

Structure keys: parent, children, naming

KeyTypeWhen omittedDescription
parentObjectnilsame as calling parent:AddChild(self) right after construction. Required for a top-level control (usually Chili.Screen0); an orphan is never drawn and never receives input
childrentable{}child list, must be an array ({ a, b, c }); array order is stacking order (later children are on top). A keyed table does nothing
namestringclassname + countercontrol name, used by GetChildByName / childrenByName; a duplicate name under the same parent raises an error
classnamestringlowercased class nameselects the skin (skin[classname]); normally leave it alone
clientWidth / clientHeightnumbernilinner (client) width/height; converted to width / height using padding, safer than doing the arithmetic yourself
minimumSizetable {w, h}nillegacy spelling of minWidth + minHeight

Geometry keys: position and size

KeyTypeWhen omittedDescription
xnumber | string0left edge inside the parent client area; negative counts from the right, a string is a percentage
ynumber | string0top edge; negative counts from the bottom, a string is a percentage
widthnumber | stringdefaultWidth of the classwidth; can be omitted when both x and right are given (stretches horizontally)
heightnumber | stringdefaultHeight of the classheight; can be omitted when both y and bottom are given (stretches vertically)
rightnumber | stringnilright edge: distance from the parent right border (right alignment); recomputed when the parent resizes
bottomnumber | stringnilbottom edge: distance from the parent bottom (bottom alignment); recomputed when the parent grows

Rule: give two of x / width / right and two of y / height / bottom; the framework derives the missing one. See the geometry rules.

More universal keys: font, hit testing, legacy aliases, merge rules, keys that do nothing expand
KeyTypeDescription
fonttablefont table, merged field by field with the class default: writing only { size = 20 } keeps the default color and outline
noFontbooleando not create a Font object (saves memory when you draw text yourself); do not combine with text properties
objectOverrideFontFontshare an existing Font instance instead of creating one
hitTestAllowEmptybooleanclicks on empty spots of the client area still count as this control (blank panels that need OnClick)
noClickThroughbooleanswallow clicks outside the client area instead of passing them on (modal overlay)
disableChildrenHitTestbooleanskip hit testing of children (all clicks land on this control)
snapToGridbooleansnap to the grid while dragging (Tweak edit mode)
Legacy aliases—fontSize / fontsize → font.size, textColor / captionColor → font.color, fontOutline → font.outline, fontShadow → font.shadow, borderColor1 → borderColor

Three most common traps: (1) visible = false is overwritten by SetParent when the control is attached, so call :Hide() afterwards; (2) there is no layer field — stacking comes from the parent children order (use :SetLayer(n) / :BringToFront()); (3) there are no center / dock / anchor keys (use percentages or a LayoutPanel). See keys that do nothing.

ClassLabel

Defined in Controls/label.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 10 · available properties 60 · own methods 4 · available methods 109
InheritanceObject→Control→Label

Static text label that measures its text and resizes itself when autosize is enabled

Overview / Controls / Button

ClassButton

Defined in Controls/button.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 8 · available properties 60 · own methods 5 · available methods 109
InheritanceObject→Control→ButtonsubComboBoxImageTabBarItem

Base button control that tracks the pressed state and repaints; the visual itself is supplied by the skin/theme

They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / TextBox

ClassTextBox

Defined in Controls/textbox.lua:11 · Parent:EditBox · own props 13 · available properties 82 · own methods 1 · available methods 122
InheritanceObject→Control→EditBox→TextBox

Read-only multi-line text box (inherits EditBox) that shows wrapped text, usually inside a ScrollBox

ClassCheckbox

Defined in Controls/checkbox.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 12 · available properties 64 · own methods 5 · available methods 109
InheritanceObject→Control→Checkbox

Checkbox control that toggles checked on click and fires OnChange; box and text visuals come from the theme

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

ClassTrackbar

Defined in Controls/trackbar.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 11 · available properties 63 · own methods 9 · available methods 112

Trackbar control: converts the mouse position into a value between min and max, rounded to step. Inherits from Control.

ClassColorbars

Defined in Controls/colorbars.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 5 · available properties 58 · own methods 5 · available methods 109
InheritanceObject→Control→Colorbars

Color bars control: four horizontal bars adjust the RGBA components and a swatch on the right previews the color. Inherits from Control.

Overview / Controls / ScrollPanel

ClassScrollPanel

Defined in Controls/scrollpanel.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 12 · available properties 65 · own methods 20 · available methods 112
InheritanceObject→Control→ScrollPanel

Scrollable container control: shows scrollbars when the content exceeds the client area and supports smooth scrolling. Inherits from Control.

Overview / Controls / LayoutPanel

ClassLayoutPanel

Defined in Controls/LayoutPanel.lua:14 · Parent:Control · own props 26 · available properties 80 · own methods 28 · available methods 126
InheritanceObject→Control→LayoutPanelsubGridImageListViewStackPanelTabBar

Base class for all auto-layout panels (grid, stackpanel, tables, itemlistview and friends); it lays out children through a shared cell table.

maxItemWidthnumber0Upper bound for child width in pixels, used as a reference limit when autoArrangeH distributes free space; 0 means unlimited.
minItemHeightnumber1Minimum child height in pixels. Default 1.
maxItemHeightnumber0Upper bound for child height in pixels, used as a reference limit when autoArrangeV distributes free space; 0 means unlimited.
autosizebooleanfalseWhen true, the panel resizes its own height to the layout result (Resize is called at the end of _LayoutChildren). Default false.
rowsnilnilForced row count; together with columns it determines the grid split (only used in resizeItems mode). nil means derive automatically.
columnsnilnilForced column count; nil means derive automatically (from ceil(sqrt(child count)) or back-computed from rows).
orientationstring"horizontal"Layout direction, either "horizontal" or "vertical". Default "horizontal".
autoArrangeHbooleanfalseWhen true, leftover horizontal space in a line is shared among cells by the "level the shortest cells first" algorithm (source marks this FIXME rename).
autoArrangeVbooleanfalseWhen true, leftover vertical space is shared among lines by the same "level the shortest lines first" algorithm (source marks this FIXME rename).
gridbooleanfalseWhen true every row must hold the same number of columns (table layout); a source comment notes this is not implemented yet.
resizeItemsbooleanfalseWhen true, _LayoutChildrenResizeItems is used and all children are stretched to fill the clientArea grid; when false, children are flowed at their own sizes.
centerItemsbooleantrueWhen true (and the cell is larger than the child), the child is centered inside its cell and leftover line space is distributed centered. Default true.
weightedResizebooleanfalseWhen true, space is distributed in proportion to each child's weight instead of equally; a missing weight counts as 1.
selectablebooleanfalseWhen true, children can be selected with the mouse. Default false.
multiSelectbooleantrueWhen true, multi-selection is allowed (with the shift/ctrl keys). Default true.
selectedItemstable{}Set of selected children, shaped like { [itemIdx] = true }.
OnSelectItemevent table{}Event table (list of listeners) fired when a child's selection state changes; callback receives (itemIdx, selected).
OnDrawItemevent table{}Placeholder callback for drawing a single child's background; the source marks it FIXME and the base class never calls it.
OnDblClickItemevent table{}Event table fired when a child is double-clicked; callback receives (itemIdx) (ImageListView passes items[itemIdx], itemIdx).
_rowsnilnilInternal field: the row count actually computed during layout, written by _LayoutChildrenResizeItems (internal).
_columnsnilnilInternal field: the column count actually computed during layout (internal).
_cellsnilnilInternal field: layout rectangle table {x, y, w, h} per child, relative to clientArea, used for drawing and hit testing (internal).

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / Grid

ClassGrid

Defined in Controls/grid.lua:1 · Parent:LayoutPanel · own props 3 · available properties 80 · own methods 0 · available methods 126
InheritanceObject→Control→LayoutPanel→Grid

Equal-cell grid container, a LayoutPanel subclass that stretches all children into an evenly sized row/column grid.

Properties 3 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"grid"Class name string, "grid", used to identify the control type.
resizeItemsbooleantrueFixed to true: children are stretched to fill the grid instead of keeping their own size.
itemPaddingtable {4 items}{0, 0, 0, 0}Cell padding fixed to {0, 0, 0, 0}, so children sit flush against the cell edges.

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / StackPanel

ClassStackPanel

Defined in Controls/stackpanel.lua:3 · Parent:LayoutPanel · own props 6 · available properties 80 · own methods 2 · available methods 126
InheritanceObject→Control→LayoutPanel→StackPanel

Single-column (or single-row) stacking container, a LayoutPanel subclass that arranges children along orientation.

Properties 6 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"stackpanel"Class name string, "stackpanel", used to identify the control type.
orientationstring"vertical"Stacking direction; default "vertical" (stacked top to bottom), can be set to "horizontal".
resizeItemsbooleantrueFixed to true: children are stretched along the stacking direction to fill the available space.
itemPaddingtable {4 items}{0, 0, 0, 0}Cell padding fixed to {0, 0, 0, 0}.
itemMargintable {4 items}{5, 5, 5, 5}Outer margin per child {left, top, right, bottom} in pixels. Default {5, 5, 5, 5}.
noFontbooleantrueInherited from Control: when true no font object is created (pure layout container that renders no text). Defaults to true.

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / ImageListView

ClassImageListView

Defined in Controls/imagelistview.lua:3 · Parent:LayoutPanel · own props 13 · available properties 85 · own methods 9 · available methods 131
InheritanceObject→Control→LayoutPanel→ImageListView

Image list view, a LayoutPanel subclass that scans a VFS directory and shows images as "icon + filename" items with directory navigation and selection.

Properties 13 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"imagelistview"Class name string, "imagelistview", used to identify the control type.
autosizebooleantrueFixed to true: the view resizes its own height to the flow layout result.
autoArrangeHbooleanfalseSwitch for automatic distribution of horizontal leftover space. Default false.
autoArrangeVbooleanfalseSwitch for automatic distribution of vertical leftover space. Default false.
centerItemsbooleanfalseFixed to false: children are not centered inside their cells.
iconXnumber64Icon item width in pixels. Default 64; the item control is iconX+10 wide.
iconYnumber64Icon item height in pixels. Default 64; the item control is iconY+20 tall.
itemMargintable {4 items}{1, 1, 1, 1}Outer margin per child {left, top, right, bottom}. Default {1, 1, 1, 1}.
selectablebooleantrueFixed to true: items can be selected with the mouse.
multiSelectbooleantrueFixed to true: shift/ctrl multi-selection is allowed.
itemstable{}Item name list of the current directory: the first entry is always '..', followed by subdirectories and then image files.
dirstring''Directory path currently scanned (a VFS path). Defaults to an empty string; the constructor immediately calls SetDir with it.
OnDirChangeevent table{}Event table fired when the directory changes; callback receives the new directory path as directory.

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / Progressbar

ClassProgressbar

Defined in Controls/progressbar.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 13 · available properties 64 · own methods 7 · available methods 113
InheritanceObject→Control→Progressbar

Progress bar control: fills a block between min and max according to value and draws a centered caption. Inherits from Control.

Properties 13 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"progressbar"Control class name, fixed to "progressbar"
defaultWidthnumber90Default width in pixels (90); used when width is not set explicitly
defaultHeightnumber20Default height in pixels (20); used when height is not set explicitly
minnumber0Lower bound of the progress range; default 0

valuenumber100Current progress value; default 100, always clamped to min..max
orientationstring"horizontal"Orientation: "horizontal" (default) or "vertical"

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

Overview / Controls / TreeViewNode

ClassTreeViewNode

Defined in Controls/treeviewnode.lua:3 · Parent:Control · own props 13 · available properties 66 · own methods 23 · available methods 118
InheritanceObject→Control→TreeViewNode

Tree node control, a Control subclass handling child add/remove, expand/collapse, recursive lookup, collapse-button clicks and per-row drawing.

Properties 13 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"treeviewnode"Class name string, "treeviewnode", used to identify the control type.
paddingtable {4 items}{16,0,0,0}Left padding {16,0,0,0}: the width in pixels reserved for the collapse triangle button; set to {0,0,0,0} when the node is root.
autosizebooleantrueFixed to true: UpdateLayout resizes the node to the total height of its children.
captionstring"node"Caption text of the node. Default "node".
expandedbooleantrueWhether the node is expanded. Default true; when collapsed the children move into _nodes_hidden and take no part in layout.
rootbooleanfalseWhether this is the root node. Default false; a root node has no collapse button, does not draw itself and ignores expand/collapse.
nodestable{}List of child nodes stored as weak links; whether a child enters it is controlled by AddChild's isNode argument.
treeviewnilnilThe owning TreeView (a weak link; New asserts that it is supplied).
_nodes_hiddentable{}Internal field: child controls moved out of children while collapsed, moved back on expand (internal).
OnSelectChangeevent table{}Event table fired when the selection state changes; callback receives (selected) (triggered by TreeView:Select).
OnCollapseevent table{}Event table fired first thing when the node is collapsed.
OnExpandevent table{}Event table fired first thing when the node is expanded.
OnDrawevent table{}Custom drawing callback; when a listener returns true, the default DrawNode is skipped.

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). Overview / Controls / TabBarItem

ClassTabBarItem

Defined in Controls/tabbaritem.lua:3 · Parent:Button · own props 4 · available properties 61 · own methods 2 · available methods 109
InheritanceObject→Control→Button→TabBarItem

Single tab button in a tab bar: notifies its parent TabBar to select it when clicked. Inherits from Button.

Properties 4 declared here

PropertiesTypeDefaultDescription
classnamestring"tabbaritem"Control class name, fixed to "tabbaritem"
captionstring'tab'Tab label; default 'tab'. The parent TabBar matches the selection by it
heightstring"100%"Height; default "100%", i.e. fills the parent
noFontbooleanfalseWhen true the text is not drawn; default false

One more key group is not listed here: the universal keys (x y width height right bottom · parent children name classname ...). They belong to no class and every control accepts them, so they are documented once, on Control and in the tutorial: universal keys on Control · What you can pass to New (Detailed information).

ClassTabBar

Defined in Controls/tabbar.lua:3 · Parent:LayoutPanel · own props 12 · available properties 83 · own methods 3 · available methods 127
InheritanceObject→Control→LayoutPanel→TabBar

Tab bar control: creates a TabBarItem per tabs entry and manages the selection. Inherits from LayoutPanel.

Compatibility shim (added by this project): stock Spring/Recoil has no Zero-K LuaRules/Utilities layer, so this file fills in the missing Spring.Utilities.CopyTable, Spring.ScaledGetMouseState, Spring.GetViewSizes and Spring.Orig at the very start of the framework load; existing functions of the same name are never overwritten, so the directory also stays ZK-compatible.

Overview / Chili UI Reference / core.lua

Modulecore.lua

69 lines · exported functions 0

Framework entry point: sets CHILI_DIRNAME/SKIN_DIRNAME, VFS.Includes the headers and controls in order, and returns Chili.

This file exports no functions; it only holds data structures / , constant definitions or include logic.

Skins 11

Chili appearance is driven by skin data: each skin.<classname> table supplies colors, textures, fonts and margins for that control, and Handlers/skinhandler.lua merges them into the instance at construction time (fill-only); DrawControl then paints from those fields. So switching skins has two meanings: (1) pick one of the bundled sets (all 11 are listed below with their actual fields), (2) write your own. Both, the three scopes (global / per class / per control) and why existing controls do not change are explained in the skins guide; the runnable demo is LuaUI/Widgets/chili_demo_09_skins.lua.

Skininfo.nameClass blocksNotes
defaultdefault19The framework fallback: a block for nearly every control, pale blue fill with black text.
BlueprintBlueprint15Blueprint style with cyan outlines.
BubbleBlackBubbleBlack2Pure black bubbles, the fewest blocks (2).
CarbonCarbon17Dark tech look with cyan highlights.
DarkGlassDarkGlass3Minimal dark glass.
DarkHiveDarkHive14Very dark grey, good for HUDs and overlays.
DarkHiveSquareDarkHiveSquare3Square-cornered variant of DarkHive, very few blocks.
EvolvedEvolved47The default (current theme value): orange focus highlight, dark panels, the most class blocks (48).
GlassGlass20Translucent glass look with blue highlights.
RobocracyRobocracy22Orange-yellow highlight, ships its own 14px font.
TwilightTwilight7Dark teal fill with cyan borders.

The default skin comes from theme.skin.general.skinName in Themes/theme.lua; the current value is "Evolved".
